name: Argument Density Score
description: Measures the ratio of distinct claims and premises against total word count
mechanism: This method evaluates the informational efficiency of a text. When instructed to generate long texts, LLMs frequently engage in 'argumentative padding'—producing verbose paragraphs that circle around a single main point without introducing novel claims, evidence, or nuance. By extracting the total number of distinct argumentative propositions (claims, premises, backing) and computing their ratio to the physical length of the text, this method yields an 'argument density score.' High word counts with an unsustainably low number of distinct propositions strongly indicate the syntactic fluff typical of an AI attempting to meet length constraints, whereas human experts tend to write with much higher, denser informational efficiency.
parameters:
Analysis type: Proposition extraction
Media: Text
Input: Formatted/Raw text
Minimum length: 150 words
Output: Argument density score (0-100)
Processing: Semantic claim extraction
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-85%. Highly accurate on essays, op-eds, and academic papers.
useCase: Detecting overly verbose AI-generated text that sounds persuasive but lacks the dense layering of actual substantive claims typical of human experts.
strengths:
• Targets the fundamental 'hallucination avoidance' padding behavior of LLMs
• Very effective at analyzing long-form content
• Independent of specific vocabulary choices
limitations:
• Susceptible to human writers practicing 'word count padding' (e.g., students)
• Ineffective on naturally sparse genres like poetry or minimalist fiction
• Requires accurate propositional parsing logic

references.title: Stab, C. & Gurevych, I. (2017). Parsing Argumentation Structures in Persuasive Essays. Computational Linguistics.
